The module hides the complexity of the full AXI4-Lite protocol.

results.summary_before: This design implements hardware logic to convert Unicode code points between UTF-8, UTF-16, and UTF-32 encodings. It detects and signals errors such as overlong encodings, out-of-range code points, and invalid byte sequences, with an option to disable range checking for the original UTF-8 specification. The design is tested via a Python test suite covering a comprehensive set of cases, and it is intended for use in any device that processes Unicode text. The documentation is thorough, describing the error signals and test methodology.

results.summary_before: This project includes a sky130-compatible standard cell generator, several demo cells, and a Tiny Tapeout design for testing them. The test design compares factory-provided cells with custom-generated cells (mux2i_2, maj3_2, dlrtp_1, dfrtp_1) using input pins for simple tests, and also supports advanced tests with a shift register, ring oscillator, and trigger pin. The documentation is sparse, with a 'TODO' for how it works, but the testing procedure is described in detail. The project is notable for combining cell generation with on-chip testing and includes cocotb tests.

results.summary_before: This project is a minimal coarse-grained reconfigurable array inspired by AMD's AI engine architecture, containing a 2x2 array of compute tiles connected by a simplified packet-switched network-on-chip. Two interface tiles connect the array to external memory and a host, and packets are routed through the NoC and processed in a pipelined manner. Eight data inputs, eight debug outputs and eight data outputs are exposed on the pins. The documentation does not describe a concrete test procedure, so how the design is exercised on silicon is unclear.

results.summary_before: This design proposes a pseudo random generator built from two ring oscillators whose outputs are sampled by a D flip-flop at a 10 kHz clock. OUT0 and OUT1 are described as complementary random outputs. The documentation says only that power should be connected and that the oscillators will in theory start oscillating. No external hardware is required, but the design is speculative and no silicon results are reported.
